Vesper tucks the key safely into her satchel and drops her voice to a whisper. "Thank you for the quiet, big fellow, I'll try not to wake you." She wades into the Keepers' gallery, keeping the lamp's gold at her back, and follows the river air up toward the Water-Stair to catch Odalie and find the Reeve before Ashgrove thinks to circle the hill.

"DM: when I get out, can I still hear the bell in town, and is Brannoc Vell's watch answering it yet?"

entries.text:
The gallery climbs in cold, ankle-deep steps, and the lamp's gold shrinks behind you to a coin and then to nothing. Your darkvision does the rest. The tunnel joins the Water-Stair at the landing under the carved lantern arch, and you find Odalie there, sitting on the bottom step with her back against the wall, breathing like a bellows. She has gone no farther, and she is not pretending otherwise. Seeing your own face drop away from yours in the dark, because the spell is still on you, she gives a thin laugh. "Don't walk about wearing me, child. It's unnerving."

The bell has stopped. No one is ringing it now, and its last echoes died while you were underground. In its place the town has found its own voice. Drifting up the stair from below you can hear it: a hand-drum beating from the Grand Quay, a horn blown twice, dogs, and doors banging. Lantern light is moving on the hill road. It looks like a line of six or seven, and it climbs steadily, with a heavier tread than a mob. That is the Harbour Reeve's watch, answering the bell. At the foot of the road, a shouted argument rises over the rest, and you catch Sorrel Thack's wheedling voice: "...by order, Reeve, a private matter of the shrine..."

Above, faintly, the ram has started again on the iron-bound door.

One thing to flag as the DM, because I'd rather say it than let it slide: your sheet now lists Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin, and your rapier and Ashgrove's written orders are missing from your pack. I have no record of any of that in our story. You can tell me what they are and what happened, and I'll fix the record to match.

The gallery is cold, ankle-deep and slick, and it climbs in a long, patient slope. The lamp's gold shrinks behind you to a coin and then a spark. The Sleeper's slow breathing follows you for a good while, a tide in the stone, before the drip of the Water-Stair replaces it. You come out at the landing under the carved lantern arch. The two bound raiders are still on their crates in the cellar above, and one of them stares down at you through the grate and decides not to make a sound.

To answer your question: the bell has stopped. You rang it until you left the rope, and nobody has taken it up since. But the town has heard it, and Marrowmere is not quiet now. Through the boarded gap at the foot of the stair, and above the river's hush, you can hear voices rising up the hill. Doors are banging and a dog is going frantic. Somewhere near the Grand Quay a watchman's whistle shrills twice, and then again, answered from another street.

Whether it's the Reeve's watch or Sorrel Thack's is harder to tell. A line of lantern light is moving along the lower hill road, perhaps six or eight lamps, and you can make out the stiff, bunched look of men who weren't expecting to be walking uphill. They're slowing near the foot of the road, where Thack's two men stand. Above, torches move behind the shrine's broken front door, and Ashgrove's raiders are shouting orders to one another.

Odalie and Old Mags's house are at the bottom of the stair, and you have about fifty minutes of Disguise Self still on your face, with no spell slots left. One note: your sheet currently shows your rapier missing from your gear. Do you want to look into that before you go on?

entries.text:
The sheet shows a few things I have no record of in play: you're a level-2 bard with 13/15 HP and 425 XP, no rapier, and a "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" in your pack. I'll go with the sheet. If you can tell me where the pin came from, I'll write it into the story properly.

The Keepers' gallery is a cold, ankle-deep crawl. The water slaps your boots, and the gold of the lamp shrinks behind you to a coin and then to nothing. Your darkvision does the rest. The gallery climbs in long, patient slopes, and the roof drips onto your hood. Twice you pass carved niches with the stubs of old candles. Once there's a bone-white handprint pressed into the clay of the wall, small as a child's. You don't stop for it.

It's about a dozen minutes of wading before the air turns sharp with river and pitch, and you find the landing under the carved lantern arch. Below you a lamp flickers: Odalie's, a stub of candle, and her voice, hoarse, saying your name once like a prayer. She's waiting, ten steps down, with her hand on the wall.

And yes, the bell. It isn't Odalie ringing it now. Someone else has taken the rope, and the strokes are quick and uneven, but they ring on through the hill. Under it, faint and thin from the town below, you hear what you hoped for: a watch rattle, a shouted order, and boots on cobbles by the dozen. A hundred voices rather than six, from the sound of it. The town woke up and came out of its houses. Whether Brannoc Vell's watch is in front of them, you can't tell from here.

You're a few steps from the cellar, the river-door and Eel Row. Ashgrove is above you with a ram and a key she doesn't have.

Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

entries.text:
Before I go on, a note as DM. Your sheet now reads differently from what I've played so far. It shows level 2 numbers (15 max HP, 3 first-level slots, all spent), no rapier, a brass lantern key, and an item called "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" that I have no record of. I'm treating the sheet as the truth. That means you have no slots to cast with right now, 2 Bardic Inspiration, and a key in your pack that I'll come back to, because it matters to this scene.

On the barrels, the sentry's crossbow follows you but doesn't fire. Ashgrove's smile widens by a hair at the laugh. Out on the dark bank, Ysolt sees your two fingers and goes perfectly still.

"A cup of your own," Ashgrove says, amused. "Of course. Dessa, take the girl's knife, and the skiff's rope. Miss Thorne is a guest." A woman with a boathook steps out and relieves you of your dagger without roughness, and the sentry lowers his crossbow a finger's width.

"You'll find I have a very simple offer," Ashgrove goes on, standing aside from the cabin door so the lamplight falls across a table, a steaming kettle and two tin cups. "The satchel is there. So is your honest face, which I admire. Say the Keepers' words to me when the moon is dark, and I will see that Marrowmere stays dry, that Sister Odalie is left her bell, and that you are paid in more gold than a foundling should ever see." Her gloved hand turns palm up, gentle as a priest. "Or refuse, and I will find another way to learn them. I'd rather it wasn't through the old woman."

Behind her, in the cabin's shadow, you count two more men at the table, and on the wall hangs a lantern shuttered to a sliver. Upriver, Corvin's song cracks and wanders on.

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

Ashgrove laughs, a real laugh, bright and short. "Bring the cup, by all means. Bring your tail too, dear. Everyone knows where it goes when you lie."

features: Darkvision: You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Hellish Resistance: You have resistance to fire damage.

Infernal Legacy: You know the thaumaturgy cantrip. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the hellish rebuke spell as a 2nd-level spell once with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. When you reach 5th level, you can cast the darkness spell once with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

Bardic Inspiration (d6): You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.  Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. At level 2: Bardic Inspiration die d6.
Jack of All Trades: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

Song of Rest (d6): Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.  The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level. At level 2: extra 1d6 hit points.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

line:
Level up! New spell: Healing Word, since I've nearly died once already and a heal at range beats a prayer. No swaps, and I'll take the fixed 6 hit points, because I don't trust my luck with a d8 after that natural 1 at the hulk.

Then she holds up the key to the lantern light. "Corvin, drop us at Tanner's Stair by dawn. Ashgrove means to open the Weeping Locks at the new moon and drown the lower town, so I need Odalie, the Reeve, and a way to break that lock before then."

entries.text:
A correction first, because the sheet knows something my narration didn't. You're already level 2, with 425 XP, so there is no level-up to take at this moment, and Healing Word is already on your list of spells known. Level 3 needs 900 XP. I'm sorry for the muddle. Your fixed-HP choice stands as a good instinct for next time.

Two more things the sheet shows. Your rapier is gone. The sentry took it from the barrel on the hulk and it stayed there when you dived out, so you have only your dagger now. And the sheet lists "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin", which I have no record of putting in your hands. I won't invent where it came from. Tell me if you know, and otherwise I'll treat it as something to figure out from the sheet.

The *Plump Heron* poles upriver through the last of the night. You doze on the wool bales under Corvin's second-best cloak, still damp and still clutching the key, and wake to grey light on the water and the stink of hides. It's dawn on Day 4. Tanner's Stair is ahead, and the shrine hill above it has a calm line of chimney smoke.

You have 13 of 15 hit points and no spell slots, as it's not yet been a night's rest. Five nights remain before the new moon. Corvin hands you a heel of bread and says nothing for once. Piet is already on the landing, looking up the stair.

What does Vesper do?

sheet.name: Vesper Thorne
sheet.opening: Vesper Thorne, a violet-skinned tiefling bard and con artist (chaotic neutral, CHA 17, rapier, lute, Sleep, Charm Person, Disguise Self, Faerie Fire, Vicious Mockery, Minor Illusion), is a level-1 character. Backstory (must stay true): found as a toddler in a fish crate on the steps of the shabby Shrine of the Lantern Saint in the river town of Marrowmere; raised by overworked Sister Odalie, who taught her scripture and never quite caught her stealing, and who gave her her first silk scarf (Vesper keeps that scarf in her pack always, never parted with, even while wearing newer scarves over her curling horns). Vesper worked the pews on feast days, then market stalls. At sixteen she left in the night with the shrine's silver offering bowl, never sold it, still carries it polished in her pack, and means to return it someday; the debt to Odalie is bigger than the bowl. Ideal: freedom, no one writes her script. Flaw: cannot resist a mark too sure of themselves even when walking away is smarter. Her tail twitches when she lies so she keeps it tucked under her coat; gold eyes look too honest. She never tells the same story twice and will cheat anyone but never a friend. Carries 15 gp, leather armor, rapier, dagger, lute, a stolen reliquary bearing another faith's saint, an annotated prayer book. Opening suggestion: Vesper is on the road some days from Marrowmere, arriving at the river-crossing village of Hollin Ford at dusk, mid-con, working a loud, overconfident merchant (exactly the kind of mark she can't resist) at the ferry inn with a fake relic story, when a wounded courier stumbles in clutching a sealed satchel and a message that names the Shrine of the Lantern Saint, or news arrives that Marrowmere's river shrine is in trouble. Something has just happened that pulls both her con and her unpaid debt to Odalie into the story, and forces her to choose between cheating the mark and acting. Invent all further names, places and details; use only SRD-compatible creatures and magic.
